text:
Sam: FYI hit a weird production mismatch when stitching two models in a pipeline: model A served with int8-kv-format v1 and model B loaded with per-layer 4bit kv scales. The KV cache rehydrate between models caused noticeable token drift.
Priya: ouch. so the cache serialization wasn't compatible across quant formats?
Sam: yes - we were naively reusing the binary cache blob between models. The attention indices looked fine but the scaled dot-products were off.
Arjun: that makes sense. different quant schemes imply different scale/zero-point semantics for keys/values. We need an explicit KV compatibility contract in manifests, not best-effort.
Sam: proposal: add a manifest field kv_cache_profile with a versioned enum and optional conversion hint. Example:
```json
{"kv_cache_profile":"per_layer_scale_v2","allowed_compat":["per_layer_scale_v1","fp16_kv"],"auto_requant":{"enabled":true,"strategy":"merge-scales","max_cost_ms":50}}
```
Priya: good. two operational questions: 1) who pays for on-the-fly conversion latency? 2) how do we detect incompatible pipelines early (CI/canary)?
Arjun: 1) loader can include max_kv_convert_ms, runtime can accept/decline. Convert is on the loader path during model swap; if declined, fallback options: host fallback or reject pipeline. 2) runtime should expose runtime.kv_compat_check(manifest_header) that can be called in CI to simulate convert cost and report compat matrix.
Sam: For errors we should have a clear code so agents can auto-fix: e.g. QUANT_KV_INCOMPAT with suggested_profile list. Example payload:
```json
{"error":"QUANT_KV_INCOMPAT","message":"kv profile mismatch: per_layer_scale_v2 != per_layer_scale_v1","suggested":["auto_requant","fp16_kv"]}
```
Priya: observability: emit kv_convert_time_ms, kv_compat_ok boolean, kv_mismatch_count, pipeline_reject_rate. Tag metrics with pipeline_id, model_versions, device_type. Ops wants alerts if pipeline_reject_rate > 0.5% over 10m.
Arjun: Also add a cheap compatibility fingerprint: runtime.kv_fingerprint(profile) -> short hex. At handshake we compare fingerprints before deciding to reuse blob. If differs we run conversion if allowed.
Sam: QA: need a harness that spins two models with different kv profiles and asserts identical outputs after conversion within threshold. Also add regression test where conversion fails (e.g., scale overflow).
Priya: security note: conversion implies touching raw weights - make sure conversion runs in a sandboxed CPU thread and honors KMS policies for private models. Add a permission in manifest: kv_conversion_allowed: true/false.
Arjun: migration plan: 1) add kv_cache_profile to manifest schema and runtime.kv_compat_check API, 2) enable canary where runtime rejects incompatible pipelines instead of silently converting, 3) after 2 weeks of low rejects, enable auto_requant conversion for opted-in customers.
DevOpsBot: canary: "deployed kv-compat check + manifest schema v1 to canary cluster" :rocket:
Sam: I'll draft the manifest schema PR and the RFC appendix. Priya: i'll add metrics + alert rules. Arjun: i'll implement kv_fingerprint and a lightweight convert path (merge-scales) with timeout.
Priya: timeline? canary by EOD Friday?
Arjun: aiming for Friday canary, need QA harness done by Thurs.
Sam: tagging @eng-runtime and @sre. Closing once manifests PR is opened. Priya: thanks all :thumbsup:
